clue.text: Given dinner, about to swallow salad plant that's going to spoil

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for being given dinner goes round the rest

parts.note: someone given dinner has been fed
to swallow food is to eat it
a herb such as basil or chives goes in a salad

explanation.surface: A diner is about to eat a salad leaf that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's going to' is padding between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To featherbed someone is to pamper or cosset them, which is to spoil them.

clue.text: Cut up over Clementine's father being a testy character

indicators.note: over means placed above in a down answer, so the first piece sits on top of the second
up in a down clue means the word for cut is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to axe is to cut
in the song Oh My Darling, Clementine, her father was a miner, forty-niner

explanation.surface: Someone upset about Clementine's dad is getting irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'testy' suggests tetchy, but here it means one who tests.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner is someone who sets and marks tests, literally a person who tests.

clue.text: Yank violent criminal out of hospital

indicators.note: out of means the hospital letter is taken away from the criminal

parts.note: a thug is a violent criminal

explanation.surface: An American hoodlum is let out of hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American, but it is a verb meaning pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank and to tug both mean to pull sharply.

clue.text: For climbing, head into the old wood

indicators.note: climbing in a down answer means reading upwards, so the combined letters are reversed
into means the word for head goes inside the old word for the

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the
nob is slang for head

explanation.surface: A climber heads into an ancient forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard, very dark timber from tropical trees.

clue.text: City agency supports European with spin

indicators.note: supports means sits beneath in a down answer, so the agency goes below
with spin means turned round, so the word for a European is reversed

parts.note: a Serb is a European from Serbia
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: An intelligence agency backs a European who spins the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Brescia is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy.

clue.text: Failed to keep quiet, so produced whisky

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the word for failed contains the word for quiet

parts.note: an engine that failed is said to have died
still means quiet and calm

explanation.surface: Someone failed to keep quiet about a whisky-making operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is made by distillation, so a maker who distilled spirit produced whisky.

clue.text: In clubs, a sort of jazz rock

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
ragtime, or rag, is an early style of jazz

explanation.surface: In nightclubs a certain kind of jazz is rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks like music after 'jazz', but it is the definition: a stone outcrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A crag is a steep rugged mass of stone, a rock face.

clue.text: Box a bit, stopping to observe

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the word for a bit sits inside the other

parts.note: to observe in the sense of remark is to comment
a bit of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: A boxer spars a little, pausing to watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a verb about fighting; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A compartment is a separate enclosed section, a box within a larger space.

clue.text: Ready to sail away from Britain, moving down river

indicators.note: moving down means a letter shifts lower in a down answer, so the river letter moves further along

parts.note: a Briton overseas is abroad

explanation.surface: Someone ready to sail away from Britain, heading downriver.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers aboard a ship are on board and so set to depart.

clue.text: Fellow has to crawl endlessly in such a swamp

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for crawl is dropped

parts.note: to crawl abjectly is to grovel

explanation.surface: A man grovels his way through a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangrove swamps are tidal coastal marshes dominated by mangrove trees, so this kind of swamp takes the name.

clue.text: Wind is backing, low to moderate at first

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the little word is is read in reverse

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of moderate

explanation.surface: A weather report: the wind is backing, light to moderate initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' is a real weather term for wind turning anticlockwise, which hides its job here.
explanation.definitionFit: The simoom is a hot, dry, dust-laden wind of the Saharan and Arabian deserts.

clue.text: Family's approval returned to sexual investigator

parts.note: one's family is one's kin; the 's is a link meaning has

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word of approval is written backwards

parts.note: yes is a word of approval or assent

explanation.surface: A family's consent is sent back to a researcher of sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Kinsey was the American biologist whose reports surveyed human sexual behaviour.

clue.text: Preparing for theatre: that is something often done the wrong way

parts.note: sc., short for Latin scilicet, means that is or namely

parts.words: something often done the wrong way
parts.note: people are said to rub others up the wrong way

explanation.surface: A note on preparing for the stage: it is often done wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre' means an operating theatre, not a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons wash hands and arms thoroughly, called scrubbing up, before entering an operating theatre.

clue.text: Church contention headed off in courteous behaviour

indicators.note: headed off means the first letter of the word for contention is removed

parts.note: contention, competing with others, is rivalry

explanation.surface: A church dispute is averted by good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headed off' reads as forestalled, but it beheads the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chivalry is the knightly code of honour, now used for gallant, polite conduct.

clue.text: Vote of confidence?

parts.note: a vote of confidence is a motion backing a leader, but read as a vote cast in confidence it is one kept private

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means a show of support; the question mark lets 'confidence' mean secrecy instead.
explanation.definitionFit: In a secret ballot each voter's choice is kept confidential.

clue.text: Much-decorated pillar of the community

parts.note: sounds like a citizen with many medals, but means a carved, painted post standing for a tribe or clan

explanation.walkthrough: 'pillar of the community' is usually a respected person; here it is a literal post.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem pole is a tall carved post bearing a community's emblems.

clue.text: Such a solid relationship?

parts.note: the word describes both a regular geometric solid and a friendship without sex

explanation.walkthrough: 'solid relationship' reads as a firm partnership; the word fits a solid and a relationship separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The five regular polyhedra are the Platonic solids, and a non-sexual friendship is a Platonic relationship.

clue.text: See protected mammal properly held?

definitions.meaning: a see is a bishop's diocese, and ... is one in Somerset, England
a playful reading of the words as bat, hand, well: a cricket bat, a protected animal's name, gripped correctly

explanation.surface: Look: a protected animal being carefully handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a command to look, but it is a noun: a bishop's diocese. The second part is a whimsical split of the answer into BAT, HAND and WELL(S); bats are legally protected in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Diocese of Bath and Wells is a Church of England bishopric, and a bishop's seat is called a see.

clue.text: Add iron to mix to create robot

indicators.note: to mix means to stir together, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for building a robot: add some iron to the mixture.
explanation.definitionFit: An android is a robot built to look human.

clue.text: New baby oppressed by two nightmares

indicators.note: oppressed by means held down between, so the pieces sit inside the two letters

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
a cub is a baby animal

explanation.surface: A newborn tormented by a pair of bad dreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are demons once thought to lie on sleepers, the original sense of nightmare.

clue.text: Partially eclipsed, found immediately just as bright

indicators.note: partially eclipsed means the answer is part of the words found immediately, partly concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Something partly eclipsed was soon found to be shining as brightly as ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partially eclipsed' sounds astronomical but signals a run of letters inside 'found immediately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Undimmed means not made fainter, so something undimmed is still as bright as before.

clue.text: Dog fed a drug to effect major change

indicators.note: fed means given something to take in, so the article goes inside the word for dog

parts.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A dog is given a drug that transforms it.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to undergo or bring about a fundamental alteration, as in genetic mutation.

clue.text: Way of working article held in hands, part of the daily grind

parts.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of working

indicators.note: held in means enclosed, so the article sits inside the two hands

parts.note: L and R are the left and right hands
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A routine of work, a thing held in one's hands, part of daily drudgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily grind' suggests routine work, but molars literally grind food every day.
explanation.definitionFit: A molar is a back tooth used for grinding food, part of the chewing done each day.

clue.text: Eager to try riding horse, with weapon

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

indicators.note: riding means sitting astride, so the word for try straddles the letter for horse

parts.note: to have a go is to try
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: Someone keen to have a go at riding a horse, carrying a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces; the gun goes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho means enthusiastic, often overly keen to get stuck in.

clue.text: Agreeable binding

definitions.meaning: an agreeable person is willing to help, accommodating
binding in the sense of placing someone under a duty, putting them under an obligation

explanation.definitionFit: Obliging means helpful and willing, and it is also the present participle of oblige, to bind by duty.

clue.text: At intervals it's grand to go out for fun

indicators.note: at intervals takes every other letter of grand, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Every so often it is grand to have a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: To gad about is to roam in search of pleasure.

clue.text: Wife has to put new feathers on chicken

parts.note: W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife
in falconry, to imp is to graft new feathers into a damaged wing

explanation.surface: A wife has to refeather a hen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like the bird being refeathered, but it means a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken in the sense of coward matches a wimp, a feeble timid person.

clue.text: Cup trodden into pieces — result?

indicators.note: into pieces means smashed, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cup trampled to bits: what is the outcome?
explanation.definitionFit: An end product is the final outcome of a process, its result.
